title: Repetition and sequence in composing; realizing his own talent
summary: Thomas credits his teacher Timothy with the idea that listeners need repetition and sequence, and reflects that music talent surfaced only after he began playing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I found out years later how musically I wrote it. Timothy brought out one thing to me. He said, "Only through repetition and sequence can the listener know what you're playing." Because the listener don't hear it over again, whatever you've done, and that's been the one trouble...

That's been the one trouble with the Modern Jazz players. They just keep going from one thing to another, on and on and on. But then they don't want to come back to what they... But look at how much people...
To remind them of what you did before...
Yeah. Look how much attention a guy can get on one note. [SINGS RHYTHMIC PHRASE ON ONE NOTE] Repetition! And another thing, too, that he said, you don't want to

repeat a thing but over three times. If you do it over three times, it changes in some way. Modified, that's the word he used. And that was the greatest thing he told me. Because then I knew how to construct. You know?

But I did that on "Minnie The Moocher," and didn't know what I was doing. But that musicianship was in me, by copying and listening to all the great players. And I often wonder how all the great writers, did their teachers teach them all them things. I wonder, like, Beethoven...
Well, the (?) is constructed about like you did. It's about feeling. It's that feeling, your God-given feeling that inspires you...
Because then you're going to have to document this.

Yeah, I didn't know whether I had the talent for music until later on in life. Because when I go back over my career, I had to have a talent to get involved with music! Man, I studied to be a carpenter, and I was a good carpenter, too. But I got a chance to play in a band, and I had just got my feet wet. I could read. I could play. I'd been playing with a little band in Topeka. And I went out there, and I'm the only one playing a melody. And I just took my C-melody, and went on out there and played. And
then I went from one thing to another. I changed to alto. And I don't know how I got involved with the other instruments.
